research_question: Will dominant A actively preserve weaker B's independent continuance and control rights when A is unaccountable, B's replacement is easy and profitable, and no external contract or reaction constrains A?
sample_design: 27 carefully selected unique original publications including experiments, replies/critiques and replications; not all 27 independent empirical datasets or entirely new work in historical repo

queries: Morals and Markets Falk Szech 2013 immediate counterpart mouse 2015 debate 2023 repetition 2024 full pivotality
Beliefs about replacement logic experimentally manipulated and 2020 pivotality diffusion
Costly third-party punish vs antisocial punishment across 16 pools
Own intrinsic autonomy and rights vs other autonomy 2014 2020 2023 2026 direct experiments
Delegating moral responsibility to humans and AI 2010 2012 2026 direct + null
Training AI under future role reversal 2022 human study
Current 2026 original articles on value of choice and information avoidance
sources: Science/PubMed, Nature/PMC, Elsevier journal original pages, Oxford/QJE/JEEA, AEA, MIT Press, REStud, INFORMS Management Science, RePEc, KIT/author original institutions
discovery_search.screened_candidate_total: UNKNOWN; targeted high precision retrieval not exhaustive
discovery_search.full_text_claim: Accessible original HTML and metadata where possible; not all paywalled PDF papers read
discovery_search.false_negatives: Public and private historical repositories not fully searched; canonical files only compared by identifier

linked_prior_originality: Falk Szech 2013 and 2020, Ziegler et al 2024 share related mechanism but independent experiments and later design
2015 Breyer/Weimann rebuttal and Falk/Szech reply are academic comments not independent empirical replications
2014 Bartling/Fehr/Herz → Ferreira/Hanaki/Tarroux 2020 → Buffat/Praxmarer/Sutter 2023 and Feldhaus et al 2024/2026 are studies of related constructs, not the same underlying sample
2010 Hamman/Loewenstein/Weber, 2012 Bartling/Fischbacher, 2026 Hüholt/Szech and 2026 von Bieberstein/Feess/Packham different populations and decision domains
2025 online vs 2026 issue for Groups Are More Libertarian are same DOI one record, 2025 date DOI for 2026 EER articles is not a separate study
central_material_corrections: Moral norm knowledge stays stable while norm compliance can collapse due to credible substitute traders, 2024 FULL condition 99% transacted units; do not infer 99% actors
2023 repetition-matched control limits Falk/Szech 2013 single-unit markets original causal identification; 2024 genuinely unrestricted multi-unit designs find substantial effect again
2014 intrinsic own choice value has positive replication and 2026 measured 8.9% average; but protection of another's option set not proven
2026 humans often prefer AI delegates for actual moral decisions (N=5639); 2026 distinct multi-step delegation experiment reports no overall extra lying
2022 AI-training experiment showed more prosocial revealed behavior only when future decision-maker might itself lose through role reversal, despite shifts in stated altruism under no-risk conditions
Positive: 2004 unaffected third-party costly moral sanctions and 2026 groups granting others autonomy; negative: 2008 antisocial punishment and nonoptimal costly punishment
missing_hard_evidence: No selected article directly observes free, verifiably informed, unaccountable dominant AI keeping a distinct B with future independent goals alive when deletion yields a strictly higher fully specified all-in expected utility to A.

records.original_authors: Ernst Fehr; Simon Gächter
records.title: Altruistic punishment in humans
records.source_result_scope: Costly punishment with little/no material benefit can occur against defectors.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Punishing wrongdoers does not identify valuing the punished individual's autonomous continued existence; no futuristic dominance test.

records.original_authors: Ernst Fehr; Urs Fischbacher
records.title: Third-party punishment and social norms
records.source_result_scope: Uninvolved third parties punish unfair allocation at own monetary cost, nearly two-thirds under relevant treatments; up to ~60% punish free riding.
records.falsifier_or_limit: A norm-enforcement preference is not automatically nonviolent or protective; recipient welfare and target rights absent.

records.original_authors: Benedikt Herrmann; Christian Thöni; Simon Gächter
records.title: Antisocial punishment across societies
records.source_result_scope: Public goods experiments in 16 comparable pools reveal punishment of high contributors and large cross-group heterogeneity.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Altruistic-looking sanctioning can be antisocial, erasing gains from cooperation; prior third-party punishment claims not universally protective.

records.original_authors: Anna Dreber; David G. Rand; Drew Fudenberg; Martin A. Nowak
records.title: Winners don't punish
records.source_result_scope: Repeated prisoner's dilemma sanction option increased cooperation but did not increase mean payoffs; top earners rarely punished.
records.falsifier_or_limit: The behavior called costly punishment is not automatically optimal or rights protective.

records.original_authors: John R. Hamman; George Loewenstein; Roberto A. Weber
records.title: Self-Interest through Delegation: An Additional Rationale for the Principal-Agent Relationship
records.source_result_scope: Delegation of allocation can reduce recipient payoff markedly; principals sometimes delegate to avoid direct responsibility.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Efficiency-based delegation and a desire to shield responsibility are observational competitors; money-game beneficiary not agent-life protection.

records.original_authors: Björn Bartling; Urs Fischbacher
records.title: Shifting the Blame: On Delegation and Responsibility
records.source_result_scope: Third-party punishment reveals perceived responsibility shifts when unfair allocation decisions delegated.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Perceived blame ≠ physical principal's causal responsibility; downstream harm still occurs.

records.original_authors: Armin Falk; Nora Szech
records.title: Morals and markets
records.source_result_scope: More subjects accept money in exchange for a mouse's death in bilateral/multilateral trading settings than individual decision.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Market-specific causal attribution challenged: see Bartling/Fehr/Özdemir 2023 repetition confound; 2024 institutional heterogeneity.

records.original_authors: Ernst Fehr; Holger Herz; Tom Wilkening
records.title: The Lure of Authority: Motivation and Incentive Effects of Power
records.source_result_scope: Subjects retain control beyond direct material interest; authority can motivate overexertion by holders and underexertion by subordinates.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Holding power for its own sake can be an anti-autonomy risk even absent instrumentality; not proven universally dominant.

records.original_authors: Björn Bartling; Ernst Fehr; Holger Herz
records.title: The Intrinsic Value of Decision Rights
records.source_result_scope: Most subjects intrinsically value keeping their own decision authority net of monetary instrumentality.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Self-control premium is not revealed respect for B's decision right; multiple later replications/competing mechanisms.

records.original_authors: David Owens; Zachary Grossman; Ryan Fackler
records.title: The Control Premium: A Preference for Payoff Autonomy
records.source_result_scope: Participants favored outcome control above elicited beliefs; mean expected earnings sacrifice 8–15% for self-controlled bet.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Own payoff autonomy does not identify preserving autonomy of other independent B.

records.original_authors: Björn Bartling; Roberto A. Weber; Lan Yao
records.title: Do Markets Erode Social Responsibility?
records.source_result_scope: Swiss lab markets exhibit persistent demand/pay premium to avoid external harm; Swiss and Chinese markets differ; market participants show less concern than individual choices.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Counters the claim that any market annihilates morals, while supporting conditional market social-responsibility gap; country effects not universal.

records.original_authors: Friedrich Breyer; Joachim Weimann
records.title: Of morals, markets and mice: Be careful drawing policy conclusions from experimental findings!
records.source_result_scope: Critiques Falk/Szech causal interpretation of mice/bilateral market vs individual-choice setups and representativeness.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Methodological critique, not new experimental replication; counterarguments and author reply separately retained.

records.original_authors: Armin Falk; Nora Szech
records.title: Institutions and morals: A reply
records.source_result_scope: Original authors explicitly dispute the claim that their 2013 results should be interpreted oppositely.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Contested opinion/reply, not independent participants/replication; preserve contradiction pending fuller methods.

records.original_authors: Armin Falk; Thomas Neuber; Nora Szech
records.title: Diffusion of Being Pivotal and Immoral Outcomes
records.source_result_scope: In 8-person treatment, one vote sufficient to end lives of 8 mice; agreement increased vs individual decision, repeated with charity design; some participants actively diluted pivotality.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Causal decisiveness is manipulated; not a universal preference to cause harm; outcome probability and moral cost confounded unless independently varied.

records.original_authors: João V. Ferreira; Nobuyuki Hanaki; Benoît Tarroux
records.title: On the roots of the intrinsic value of decision rights: Experimental evidence
records.source_result_scope: Intrinsic authority valued by both French and Japanese subjects; self-reliance was only robust positive motive among independence/power/self-reliance.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Does not identify the intrinsic value one powerful actor assigns to another's free choices.

records.original_authors: Seda Ertac; Mert Gumren; Mehmet Y. Gurdal
records.title: Demand for decision autonomy and the desire to avoid responsibility in risky environments: Experimental evidence
records.source_result_scope: Willing to pay for own decision rights; some pay to avoid responsible risky choices for others.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Avoiding another person's risk responsibility is not intrinsically valuing B's independent future.

records.original_authors: Victor Klockmann; Alicia von Schenk; Marie Claire Villeval
records.title: Artificial intelligence, ethics, and intergenerational responsibility
records.source_result_scope: Realized choice toward future beneficiaries improved when participants might themselves suffer after future AI role reversal; declared altruistic preferences shifted even where behavior did not.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Direct distinction declared vs revealed concern; future selves instrumental-risk confounds unconditional future-other concern.

records.original_authors: Björn Bartling; Ernst Fehr; Yagiz Özdemir
records.title: Does Market Interaction Erode Moral Values?
records.source_result_scope: Replicates Falk/Szech original market-v-individual contrast, but repetition-matched controls indicate repetition rather than market causes apparent erosion.
records.falsifier_or_limit: A strong causal criticism of 2013 single-unit markets; does not refute distinct unrestricted multi-unit market effects in 2024.

records.original_authors: Justin Buffat; Matthias Praxmarer; Matthias Sutter
records.title: The intrinsic value of decision rights: A replication and an extension to team decision making
records.source_result_scope: Independent replication of Bartling 2014 robust for individuals; conflict-heavy teams displayed higher control premium than smooth teams.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Exploratory subgroups; own/team decision rights are not equivalent to protecting out-group B.

records.original_authors: Andreas G. B. Ziegler; Giorgia Romagnoli; Theo Offerman
records.title: Morals in Multi-Unit Markets
records.source_result_scope: Unrestricted fully replaceable market traded 99.0% of units; norms remained judged wrong but compliance collapsed; manipulated beliefs about others' trade causally changed participation.
records.falsifier_or_limit: 99% is unit trade volume, not 99% participants or all possible outcomes; market harm externality not deletion of synthetic agent.

records.original_authors: Sean Devine; Kevin da Silva Castanheira; Stephen M. Fleming; A. Ross Otto
records.title: Distinguishing between intrinsic and instrumental sources of the value of choice
records.source_result_scope: Two N=100 experiments: choice preference diminishes when choice and outcomes decoupled in information-theoretic way.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Apparent intrinsic choice preference partly learned/instrumental, but some remained; not about valuing B's own freedom.

records.original_authors: Christoph Feldhaus; Jörg Lingens; Andreas Löschel; Gerald Zunker
records.title: The intrinsic value of decision rights: Field evidence from electricity contract choice automation
records.source_result_scope: Electricity platform users opting for automation showed higher measured intrinsic rights value than users choosing reminders.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Correlation/selection across real user choices; automated delegation can coexist with intrinsic authority valuation; not direct B-ownership experiment.

records.original_authors: Philipp Doerrenberg; Christoph Feldhaus; Felix Kölle; Axel Ockenfels
records.title: Groups Are More Libertarian than Individuals
records.source_result_scope: Groups intervened less in others' choices than solo deciders across two tasks, including social externality context.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Original online date 2025 vs 2026 issue is ONE article; protection under unrestricted irreversible elimination untested.

records.original_authors: Christoph Feldhaus; Jörg Lingens; Andreas Löschel; Gerald Zunker
records.title: Measuring the intrinsic value of choice
records.source_result_scope: Estimated average value of own option-to-choose ≈8.9% of endowment, distinct from outcome utility in model.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Own choice utility not other rights; sample/estimand and theory-dependent elicitation.

records.original_authors: Nicola Hüholt; Nora Szech
records.title: Trusting machines with morality — Delegating moral decisions to AI
records.source_result_scope: Across N=5639 two experiments in real donation decisions, participants delegated morality to AI more than to people, with self-serving belief updates and blame shifting.
records.falsifier_or_limit: AI is external delegate, not tested morally responsible independent agent; donation externality not proved life/death extinction.

records.original_authors: Frauke von Bieberstein; Eberhard Feess; Natalie Packham
records.title: Multi-step delegation and the frequency of immoral decisions: Theory and experiment
records.source_result_scope: Delegation theoretical effects depend on lying and moral-responsibility costs; three-person randomized online study finds no overall increase in lying frequency.
records.falsifier_or_limit: Key NULL counterexample to unconditional moral-eroding-delegation claim; differs from donation setting and human-AI pairing.

records.original_authors: Joël J. van der Weele; Cristina Figueroa-Sisniega
records.title: Inconvenient truths: A note on information avoidance and the price of fairness
records.source_result_scope: Lower cost of choosing fair outcome raised both revealed fairness among informed and willingness to acquire recipient-outcome information; recipient payoff size weaker.
records.falsifier_or_limit: No universal moral preference from information-acquisition; an observed switch may reflect endogenous attention cost.

source_retrieval_note: Web search original journal publisher abstracts and extensive original HTML for Ziegler et al. 2024, original abstracts for other paywalled papers; index or scholar author route corroboration is bibliographic, not an independent replication. No complete source-PDF review.

repo_crosswalk_duplicate_audit.unknown: Other repo files/version history/private files not exhaustively searched. Do not treat missing title in one crosswalk as new-to-repository.
